 1. HR Technology Planning, Intake & Prioritization | 30%

 Establish the cadence, criteria, and governance used to evaluate incoming demand, assess capacity and dependencies, prioritize investments, and translate HR and Product priorities into an executable roadmap.

 Lead, develop, and set direction for a team responsible for HR technology project management, vendor management, and portfolio execution.  
 Serve as a senior HR technology leader with the executive presence to represent portfolio priorities, risks, and tradeoffs with HR and technology leadership.

 Authentic . Real connection happens when we show up as our best, truest selves, help others dothe same, and stand by each other through the harder times.
 Curious . Curiosity keeps us innovative. Better understanding comes from asking helpful questions, seeking to understand before we act, and building on each other's thinking.

 WHAT IS YOUR ROLE
 As Senior Director, People Operations, you are the operational and governance backbone of Boldr's People function. You own the systems, rewards, and standards that let a five-country division run with consistency and care.
 Three connected disciplines roll up to you across the Philippines, South Africa, Mexico, Canada, and the United States:
 People Operations and Systems : the employee lifecycle, our HRIS (Rippling), people data, service delivery, and self-service.

The longer-range strategic agenda, organizational design, performance strategy, and strategic business partnering, sits with the VP and grows alongside our People Success team. Your mandate is to make the backbone genuinely excellent: scalable processes that do not rely on heroics, clean and trustworthy data, sound compliance across every jurisdiction, and a team member experience that reflects our values wherever people work.
 You report to the VP, People, and you are one of the leaders the rest of the division depends on to keep the engine running as we scale.
 WHY DO WE WANT YOU
 We are looking for an impact-driven operator who can give a fast-growing, five-country division the backbone it needs to scale without breaking. Someone who builds systems that last, holds a high bar on compliance and fairness, and still keeps the human center in every process they design.
 You will protect organizational health, bring calm and consistency to sensitive moments, and make the everyday experience of working at Boldr feel reliable and fair in every country we operate in. We do all of this so our team members can thrive as we grow.

 People Operations and Systems
 Own the employee lifecycle end-to-end: onboarding, changes, and offboarding, delivered consistently across all five countries.
 Lead Rippling as our HRIS and system of record; design and maintain clean workflows, self-service, and service delivery (ticketing and knowledge base).
 Establish data integrity and reporting discipline: headcount, attrition, and the people data leaders rely on to decide well.

 Modernize People infrastructure through automation and sound system design, so support scales without manual workarounds.

 Direct compensation cycles with rigor and clarity: timelines, manager enablement, auditability, and clear communication.
 Oversee job banding and pay structures using our market data source (Payfactors), keeping pay equitable and defensible.
 Steward pay equity and transparency norms that build trust while managing risk appropriately.
 Employee Relations

 Build the ER frameworks and manager guidance that keep outcomes fair and well-documented across countries.
 Serve as a trusted, high-integrity escalation point on difficult people matters.
 Compliance, Risk, and Governance
 Ensure compliance across all five countries and both operating models: Managed Outsourcing and Global Employment (EoR).
 Own records, audit, and data protection for People data.
 Translate local labor realities into sound, consistent decisions, flag clearly where in-country counsel is needed, and engage and consult with counsel on these matters .
 Build the governance and risk frameworks that let us scale responsibly.

 Lead and develop the People Operations, Total Rewards, and Business Partnering teams; set clear goals, coach for growth, and build a culture of service excellence.

 WHAT LIKE ABOUT YOU

 YOU HAVE…

Program Structure and Trust is a newly chartered group at Vanta with a focused mission: build the enterprise org model that lets customers bring their compliance and security structure — product lines, business units, isolated data environments, cross-cutting audits, scoped approvals, and data residency requirements — natively into the platform. The problems this team solves determine whether Vanta can serve the enterprise customers it's increasingly winning.

 

This is the defining technical role of the group. The Staff Engineer owns the design, phased delivery, and long-term technical direction of Vanta's enterprise org model — a multi-quarter initiative that cuts across the platform and establishes the foundation for how enterprise customers structure, segment, and operate inside Vanta.

 

 
 

What you'll do as a Staff Engineer at Vanta:

 - Own the design and multi-quarter delivery of Vanta's enterprise org model, including hierarchical product lines and business units, isolated data access and ownership, cross-cutting audit workflows, scoped approvals, and EU and GovCloud data residency support

 - Define and evolve the core abstractions that let the platform absorb structurally diverse, often conflicting enterprise requirements — solving for the general case rather than one-off customer accommodations

 - Retrofit a live production system toward a multi-tenant org structure: design safe migration paths, sequence delivery incrementally, and preserve continuity for existing customers as the architecture evolves

 - Carve out and ship meaningful customer value each quarter while progressing toward the full solution — this requires product judgment, direct engagement with enterprise customers, and the discipline to draw clean increment lines through a complex problem space

 - Drive execution across squads outside your direct area, building alignment through technical clarity and credibility rather than authority

 - Partner with Engineering leadership, Product, and Design to translate the long-term vision for enterprise structure into phased, deliverable work

 - Set the technical standard for the group — define patterns others build to, shape architecture across teams, and model the engineering excellence the Program Structure and Trust charter is organized around

 

How to be successful in this role:

 - 10+ years of deep backend engineering experience with a track record of leading complex, multi-quarter technical initiatives in fast-paced, product-focused environments

 - Designed platform abstractions that absorbed messy, conflicting enterprise requirements across a diverse customer base — you've solved for the general case, not the loudest customer request

 - A track record of shipping in stages: you've moved large, structurally complex problems forward incrementally, with each phase standing on its own, without getting ahead of what customers and the product can absorb

 - A history of operating effectively across squads and teams you don't own — alignment built through technical clarity and credibility, not org chart proximity

 - Deep familiarity with enterprise architectural patterns: tenancy models, role-based access control, data isolation, scoped permissions, cross-tenant operations, and access boundary design

 - Strong communication skills — you make complex systems legible to engineering leadership, product partners, and customer-facing stakeholders, in writing and in the room

 - Data residency or GovCloud exposure is a plus; the right person ramps on this in a quarter once the core structural problems are in hand

 - Open to using AI to amplify your skills and strengthen your work - demonstrating curiosity, a willingness to learn, and sound judgment in applying AI responsibly to improve efficiency and impact.

What you can expect as a Vanta’n:

 - Industry-competitive salary and equity

 - Pension contribution

 - Health & wellness stipend

 - Remote workspace, internet, and cellphone stipend

 - Flexible work hours and location

 - 11 company-paid holidays

You'll help design the identity primitives that make autonomous agent behavior safe and governable at scale.

As a Senior Software Engineer, you'll shape the direction of these areas in the IAM pillar, and your technical decisions will create leverage across the engineering organization.

 - Architect and evolve Vanta's authentication and authorization platform, setting technical direction for how identity, permissions, and access are enforced across the entire product

 - Lead initiatives that raise the security and reliability bar for auth primitives, spanning API-layer enforcement, enterprise identity protocols (SAML, SSO, SCIM), and access control at scale

Mindrift connects specialists with project-based AI opportunities for leading tech companies, focused on testing, evaluating, and improving AI systems. Participation is project-based and is not an employment relationship.
 What this opportunity involves 
 We're looking for contributors to share their own medical lab report. You add the original files, and details that identify you, such as names, ID numbers, dates of birth, and contact details, are covered automatically and checked again during review before the report is used. You also check the redacted preview before you submit. The lab's name and address, the test names, and the results stay in the report. Once your report is accepted, it is no longer linked to you. The files help improve AI systems that read and understand medical documents. In this project, contributors may:
 Add the PDF file of their own lab report, for example blood test results;
 Take an iPhone photo of each printed page of the report and a screenshot of each page on an iPhone, iPad, or Mac;
 Check the redacted preview of each page and submit it only if all details that identify them are covered;
 Add one report per task;
 Submit clear files where every page of the report is fully visible.
 If you have your own lab test results and are comfortable sharing them once your personal details are covered, apply to take part in this project.
 What we look for 
 This opportunity is a good fit for people who have their own lab test results and are open to a short-term, project-based collaboration. To take part, contributors will need:
 To be 18 to 65 years old and live in one of these countries: the UK, Canada, Ireland, Germany, Switzerland, Poland, Portugal, Brazil, Spain, Türkiye, Norway, Indonesia, the UAE, or Israel (no VPN while using Mindrift);
 Their own medical lab report as a PDF file (1 to 10 pages): lab test results only, such as a blood count, blood chemistry, or a urine test;
 A report from a lab in the country where they live, preferably in the local language (reports in English, or in both languages, are also accepted);
 A printed copy of the report, an iPhone (any model) for the photos, and an iPhone, iPad, or Mac for the screenshots.
 This opportunity is not suitable for someone else’s lab report (for example, a family member’s), a translated or edited copy of a report, or other medical documents such as discharge summaries or surgery notes. 
 How it works  
 Apply → Get an email from Mindrift Team (check spam too) → Register on Mindrift → Verify your identity → Sign the project consent form → Add your report's PDF, photos, and screenshots and check the redacted preview → Get paid for each accepted report 
 Privacy
 Taking part is voluntary, and choosing not to take part doesn’t affect your Mindrift account. Before your first task, you read and sign a project consent form. Details that identify you, such as names, ID numbers, dates of birth, addresses, phone numbers, and email addresses, as well as doctors' names and signatures, are covered automatically and checked again during review before the report is used. Your original files are deleted. Once your report is accepted, it is no longer linked to you. We never ask you to send your report by email, chat or anywhere outside the Mindrift platform.
 Project time expectations 
 Each lab report is a separate task, and you can add reports whenever it suits you while the project is active. This is a time-limited project, and the number of reports we can accept is not guaranteed. Reports need to meet the listed criteria to be accepted. If a report needs a fix, it comes back to you with the reason. 
 Earnings  
 Paid per accepted report:  $10 for every lab report  (PDF, photos, and screenshots of each page) that passes our quality checks. Earnings are added to your Mindrift balance once the report is accepted. 
 You can withdraw them to your bank account or PayPal via Tipalti, or via Payoneer (minimum $20). Payouts are processed twice a month. Mindrift doesn't deduct any fees, but your payment provider may charge a small transfer fee.

Sadie is building technology for hospitality.
 We're looking for an account executive to win new restaurant customers in Vancouver or Calgary, and to run every deal yourself from the first lead to the signed agreement.
 This is a field role. You'll find restaurants through outbound outreach, networking and on-site visits, then meet owners in person and show them Sadie working on their own calls. You'll work with onboarding and customer success, so that what you sell goes live well. You'll carry monthly and quarterly targets and own the forecast behind them.
 You decide where to spend your time and which deals to pursue, within agreed pricing and terms. AI should be part of how you work. Use it to research restaurants before a visit, prepare demos, draft proposals and follow-ups, and plan your territory. You're responsible for the quality of everything that goes out under your name.
 What we value
 Sound judgement about which deals are real.
 Taking responsibility for your number and finishing work without being chased.
 Understanding how a restaurant makes money, and caring whether Sadie improves it.
 Curiosity about why a deal was lost, and a willingness to change your approach.
 The honesty to say a deal is slipping before the forecast says it for you.
 What you'll do
 Win new restaurants, from first visit to signed agreement 
 Most of your time goes on live deals, and most of those deals happen in person. You'll sit down with owners and general managers in their restaurants to learn how the phone is handled today: who answers it, what gets missed during service, and what those missed calls cost in bookings and orders. Then you'll demo Sadie against that picture.
 You'll scope what the restaurant needs, write the proposal, negotiate terms and get the agreement signed. 
 Most of the judgement is in qualification. A good demo with someone who can't sign, or a restaurant Sadie can't serve yet, costs you weeks. You're expected to spot that early and move on.
 Build your own pipeline across your territory 
 You'll generate your own leads through outbound outreach, networking and on-site visits. That means planning which neighbourhoods and restaurant groups to work, walking in at the right time of day, and following up until you get a meeting.
 Hit your targets with a forecast you can defend 
 You're measured against monthly and quarterly sales targets, and the expectation is that you hit them consistently. You'll keep every opportunity accurate in HubSpot, so that stage, value and close date mean something to the people who plan around them.
 Represent Sadie where restaurant people meet 
 You'll attend local industry events, restaurant meetups and trade shows across your geography. You'll decide which ones are worth the evening, run the conversations there, and turn them into meetings within the week.
 For a lot of operators, you'll be the first person from Sadie they meet. What they hear from you is what they'll repeat to other owners.
 Hand over accounts that go live well 
 The restaurant buys Sadie, but the guest ringing to book a table decides whether it works. You'll give onboarding and customer success a written record of what you promised, what the owner expects, and what could go wrong.
 If you oversell, the owner finds out on a Friday night and the guest pays for it. Set expectations you can stand behind.
 What you'll bring
 At least 2 years in a closing sales role, selling software or services to businesses in hospitality (ideally full service restaurants) or experience working at full service restaurants.
 A record of meeting targets, and the ability to explain how you did it.
 Experience running the whole cycle yourself, from prospecting through to signature.
 Comfort with in-person selling, including cold visits and demos in front of a busy owner.
 Strong discovery skills. You can find out what an operator needs in fifteen minutes between services.
 Clear written communication. Your proposals and follow-ups are accurate and short.
 An honest forecast. You'd rather call a deal lost than carry it for another month.
 You use AI every day for research, preparation and drafting, and you check what it produces.
 You organise your own week across a territory and follow through without being managed.
 Useful experience
 Selling to restaurants or other hospitality operators.
 Working in a restaurant yourself, front of house or in management.
 Selling reservations, POS, telephony or other restaurant technology.
 An existing network among restaurant owners in your territory.
 Selling AI products to non-technical buyers.
 Being an early sales hire at a startup.
 Who will enjoy this role
 You like finding out how a business really works. When an owner says they miss calls at seven on a Saturday, you want to know how many, what those calls were for, and what happened to the guest who hung up.
 In a single week you might walk into six restaurants before lunch service, run a demo at a bar between shifts, spend an evening at a trade show, and sit with onboarding to sort out an account you signed. Your schedule follows the restaurant day, and some of your best conversations will happen at three in the afternoon or late at night.
 The hard parts are specific. Owners are busy and sceptical, and many will turn you away mid-service. You'll hear no far more often than yes, and you'll still need to be back through the next door the same afternoon. Some of the material you'd expect to have, such as local case studies or a settled playbook, may not exist yet, and you'll help build it while carrying a number.
 Why this role matters
 Sadie is building technology for hospitality. Restaurants lose revenue to calls nobody picks up, and our product exists to answer them.
 This role is how Sadie reaches the restaurants in your geography. You decide who to visit and how each customer starts. The agreements you sign affect revenue, what onboarding and customer success inherit, and what a guest hears when they ring to book a table.
 You'll own new restaurant business across your territory, with the authority to decide how Sadie wins it.

Rockstar is recruiting for a mission-driven startup that builds modern technology for the aging and disability services sector. They are a women-founded, venture-backed company tackling the $100B+ social services market to enable the delivery of life-sustaining services for older adults and people with disabilities. The company's customers are large public agencies across the country who coordinate complex networks of care, but who are currently wasting 60% of their time on administrative paperwork that can be digitized and automated. Their cloud-based solutions allow these agencies to streamline workflow, increase capacity to serve more people, and track outcomes. They have raised over $15M in capital and are backed by leading VCs in healthcare and SaaS.
 About the Role
 As a Senior Engineer at the company, you're responsible for designing, building, testing, and maintaining the core software our customers rely on every day. You'll take high command of a defined area of the codebase — and work closely with product managers and a team of 1–3 junior engineers to ship the projects that move our public-agency customers forward.
 The stack is Ruby on Rails, Bootstrap, Stimulus, and Postgres. Expect to write code, review code, design data models, and mentor the people around you in roughly equal measure.
 Primary Responsibilities
 Experienced coding skill: Take high command of a defined area of the codebase, shipping production-grade Rails features end to end. Comfortable with the stack (Rails, Bootstrap, Stimulus, Postgres) or a close analog like Django.
 Develop people: Support and grow a team of 1–3 junior engineers, partnering with product managers to complete projects and develop talent in parallel.
 Startup agility and initiative: Operate inside a small, scrappy team that punches above its weight — get stuff done, figure things out, and marshal the resources you need to hit the goal.
 Engineering quality: Apply refactoring, careful data design, and disciplined testing (the team maintains a 1.4:1 test-to-code ratio) to keep the codebase healthy as it grows.
 AI-assisted development: Use tools like Claude Code or Codex fluently as a force multiplier on already strong development practices, and know when to reach for which model.
 About You
 3–5+ years of experience: You've excelled as a mid-level engineer at a fast-growing technology company.
 Rails + Postgres fluency: Solid working experience with most of: Ruby on Rails, Stimulus, JavaScript, Bootstrap, CSS3, Hotwire/Turbo, RSpec, ViewComponent, SQL/Postgres, Git, and SQL reporting tools.
 Strong engineering practices: Track record of thoughtful refactoring, careful data design, and disciplined testing.
 Creative problem-solver: Enjoy evaluating and incorporating third-party software and APIs to move faster without cutting corners.
 AI dev tool fluency: Strong hands-on experience with Claude Code, Codex, or similar — and enough familiarity with the underlying models to know when each one earns its keep.
 Agile-comfortable: Familiar and at home with Agile methodologies.
 Bonus: Experience with Terraform, AWS, and/or Google Cloud; building HIPAA-regulated products with PHI; multi-tenant SaaS architecture.
 Our Culture
 The company values high performance and high enjoyment. In addition to having the privilege of working hard on a mission they believe in, the team gets to do it with people they genuinely respect and like being around. The hybrid/remote company of ~40 gets together in person 2x per year for team-proposed activities like board games, cooking competitions, and time in nature. In between those retreats, the team makes time for 1-1 connections across the company. They have a flat hierarchy: ideas for innovation that come from interns make it into the hands of users. Founded by two women of color, the company knows diversity in the team leads to higher quality decisions, so they continually invest in recruiting from under-represented groups and maintaining an inclusive environment.
 Benefits
 The expected salary range for this position is between $130,000 and $180,000. The actual compensation will be determined based on experience and other factors permitted by law.
 Health insurance, 15 days PTO (20 days after year two), and sick leave
 401K, disability insurance, FSA, and HSA
 Generous paid family leave
 The opportunity to do work that matters with a team that treats one another with respect and kindness

 Reporting to the Manufacturing Engineering team, the successful candidate will collaborate closely with Design Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, Production, Suppliers, and Professional Field Services to deliver scalable, reliable, and efficient manufacturing solutions.

 What You Will Do

 Support production readiness reviews and ensure successful execution of project deliverables.
